clinicalPearls: A cystic lesion arising from the ductal system of the lacrimal gland (or accessory glands)
It presents as a smooth, fluctuant, sometimes bluish swelling in the region of the lacrimal gland or superolateral fornix
It may fluctuate in size and can cause a foreign-body sensation or, if large, mechanical effects
Transillumination and imaging demonstrate its cystic, fluid-filled nature
It is benign and distinct from solid lacrimal gland tumours
Management ranges from observation to marsupialisation or excision for symptomatic lesions
reference.pathophysiology: Dacryops results from cystic dilatation of a lacrimal gland duct, thought to follow ductal obstruction or a valve-like mechanism that traps secretions, leading to a fluid-filled cyst lined by ductal epithelium. Because it communicates with, or arises from, the secretory ductal system, it may enlarge with lacrimal stimulation. It is a benign cystic lesion rather than a neoplasm, which imaging and its fluctuant, transilluminating character help confirm.
additionalDifferentials: Orbital lymphangioma or other cystic orbital lesion
additionalInvestigations: Imaging (ultrasound, CT or MRI) showing a cystic lacrimal lesion
Assessment of size fluctuation and effect on the globe
Exclusion of a solid lacrimal gland tumour
Histology of the cyst wall if excised
redFlags: A solid or rapidly enlarging mass suggesting neoplasm
reference.prognosis: Dacryops is benign with an excellent prognosis; symptomatic lesions do well after marsupialisation or excision, though recurrence can occur.
pitfalls: Mistaking a solid lacrimal gland tumour for a benign cyst
Simple aspiration leading to recurrence rather than definitive marsupialisation
Attributing a fluctuant swelling to infection
management: Observe small, asymptomatic lesions, as dacryops is a benign lacrimal ductal cyst
Confirm the cystic, fluid-filled nature with transillumination and imaging (ultrasound, CT or MRI) before intervention, and exclude a solid lacrimal gland tumour
Treat symptomatic or enlarging lesions with marsupialisation or surgical excision, sending the cyst wall for histology
Counsel patients that recurrence can occur after drainage or incomplete excision, and arrange follow-up
Refer to oculoplastics for surgical planning of symptomatic lesions
